headline: The Wilderness Society, a US conservation group, has called for a halt to building AI data centers on federal public lands.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: Reuters' opening paragraphs confirm a named group's call and the federal permit context; the rest of the story could not be read.
importance_line: People who use or live near public lands, and the officials who decide on these permits, are affected, but a moratorium is only a request from an advocacy group and the permits are still under consideration.
summary: Reuters reports that The Wilderness Society, a US conservation group, called on Monday 5 Oct 2026 for a moratorium (a halt) on artificial intelligence data centers on federal lands, citing water use, electricity demand, wildlife habitat and public access. The call comes as the Trump administration is considering permits for several data center developments on land run by the Bureau of Land Management, according to federal land records cited by Reuters.
notes: Reuters page returned 401. The wording comes from Reuters' opening paragraphs on TradingView and in its US domestic news summary on Devdiscourse (three sentences); the rest of the story was not available, so the group's detailed demands and any government response are unknown.
